I only have 2.6 mu and I am 73, so I will keep things simple and steady. I will plant cotton on all of it again because that is what I know best and it matches my land and irrigation conditions. I will use improved seed, not chase anything too risky, because I want better stand establishment and more stable yield. Before sowing, I will prepare the land with rotary tillage because it is easier for me than deep ploughing and good enough for this small area. For fertilizer, I will use a moderate amount of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium so the cotton grows steadily without wasting money. Since I have well irrigation, I will irrigate a few key times if moisture is short, mainly around establishment, flowering, and boll setting, because those stages matter most for yield. I will spray pesticide only as needed through the season, but I expect several applications because cotton usually gets insect pressure. My goal is not the highest possible yield; I will manage for a stable crop that I can handle with my age, labor, and experience.
